title: publish-release.mjs reports the wrapper "published and verified" before a consumer can install it
description: Measured during the 0.7.1 publish, 2026-09-15. scripts/publish-release.mjs printed "@opum-ai/quest 0.7.1 published and verified (1 check)" and exited 0; at 16:03:02Z, seconds later, `npm install -g @opum-ai/quest@0.7.1` failed with notarget, a plain HTTPS read of registry.npmjs.org/@opum-ai/quest/0.7.1 returned "version not found: 0.7.1", the packument listed versions up to 0.7.0 with dist-tags latest 0.7.0, and the wrapper first resolved from a plain read at 16:04:06Z (packument time.modified 16:03:39Z). So the final verification passed inside a window in which a consumer install failed: the same class QCLI-299 closed for the platform packages (write success is not consumer visibility) is still open for the wrapper own post-publish verification, which apparently reads through a path that sees the write before the public read API does. Not urgent: the six platform packages were correctly gated, nothing was left uninstallable for more than about a minute, and the receipt:verify-published gate passed afterwards. It matters because the script output is what an operator stops on, and "verified" was said about a state a consumer could not yet see.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The wrapper post-publish verification reads the public registry over plain HTTPS with no credential and no npmrc, the same client the platform gate uses, and holds the same settle margin before declaring success

A test drives the failure on purpose: a wrapper whose write returned success but whose public packument does not yet list the version is reported as not-yet-visible, and the script does not print "published and verified" until a plain read resolves it
The runbook publish section states what "verified" means after this change and records the 0.7.1 measurement (about a minute between the script verification and the first public read)

implementationNotes:
HANDOFF 2026-09-17T02:35Z (date -u). Orchestrator ruling: this is the next task. Not yet started -- no branch, no code, nothing in flight.

WHY IT IS NEXT, and why it is cheap right now: it is the same defect class as QCLI-300, which just shipped -- a success message asserting more than the check measured. QCLI-300 built scripts/qualification/require-platform-visibility.mjs, a thin runner over registry-visibility.mjs (waitForConsumerVisibility, classifyVersion, describeVersionState). Whatever QCLI-304 needs for "can a consumer actually install this", that module almost certainly already does; extend or reuse it rather than writing a third implementation of the same read. Two implementations of "did it land" already exist and a third would drift.

ORDERING IN THE RELEASE-MACHINERY CLUSTER, as reported to the orchestrator and endorsed. Of the three I judged load-bearing for a next cut, QCLI-300 is now Done. Remaining: QCLI-304 (this one), then QCLI-292 (bun.lock platform pins do not update with a version bump, so it must be patched reactively every release -- the one that bites on the day of a cut). Everything else in the cluster -- QCLI-259, 275, 280, 286, 293, 295, 296, 305, 307(Paused), 308 -- I judged deferrable past a next cut. That is JUDGEMENT, not a tracker field: priority is unset on nearly all of these, so no ordering exists to read off, and a successor is free to disagree with reasons.

NAVIGATION HAZARD, worth more than it looks, and it cost this session a near-miss. The state of trusted publishing / OIDC lives in QCLI-271 notes -- 40 of them, covering both the npm Trusted Publishing immutable-subject-claim failure AND the AMFI SIGKILL on the darwin-arm64 binary. QCLI-271 TITLE is about neither ("QCLI-266 fix is landed on dev and unreleased, so every consumer still runs the broken help"), because both findings were recorded during that task rather than being what it was filed for. .github/workflows/release.yml:167 and CLAUDE.md both cite QCLI-271 and BOTH ARE CORRECT. I read the title, concluded the citations were dangling, and was about to file a defect; checking the notes showed there is none. Do not re-file it. If you need the OIDC state, read QCLI-271 notes, not its title.

CONSEQUENCE FOR QCLI-300 THAT MUST NOT BE LOST: the CI wrapper-publish gate ALREADY EXISTS on main as of today. Whoever restores trusted publishing must not rebuild it. QCLI-300 defect was dormant rather than live precisely because the CI path published neither 0.7.0 nor 0.7.1; restoring OIDC is what would have made it live, on the day nobody would have been looking. That is recorded on QCLI-300 as well.

Also unproven and stated as such on QCLI-300: that a failing step halts the job and leaves the wrapper unpublished is GitHub Actions semantics, asserted through an ordering test over release.yml plus the workflow contract, NOT executed. The first real CI publish after OIDC is restored is the first time that half runs for real.
